title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Yeovil Hybrid (4 days in office) £27,000 - £33,000 per annum

Looking for a finance role where you can learn, grow and make a real difference?

The Opportunity

Right Pear is partnering with an established Yeovil-based business to recruit an Accounts Assistant into its finance team on a permanent, full-time basis.

The business is going through an exciting period of investment and development, including a review of how its finance function works and where processes can be improved. That makes this a great time to join. You'll be part of a small, supportive team with access to experienced senior finance professionals, and you'll have the chance to shape how things are done rather than just follow a set routine.

This role suits someone early in their finance career who has a solid technical foundation and wants to keep building on it.

The Role

You'll support the day-to-day running of the finance function, working closely with the wider finance team.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Processing and posting transactions accurately in the accounting system
- Preparing and reviewing reconciliations, including balance sheet reconciliations
- Supporting month-end processes and the preparation of management information
- Building and maintaining Excel workbooks, with linked worksheets and formula-driven reporting
- Checking work carefully for accuracy and resolving discrepancies
- Following structured finance processes and suggesting ways to improve them
- Helping the business make better use of its systems and data as the finance function develops

About You

We're keen to speak with detail-focused finance professionals who enjoy getting things right and want to grow their careers.

You'll ideally have:
- AAT qualified or an equivalent background.
- Experience using Xero (Sage 50 experience is also useful)
- Strong Excel skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good verbal communication skills and confidence working with colleagues across the business
- The ability to commute to Yeovil four days a week

The Package
- £27,000 - £33,000 per annum
- Hybrid working: 4 days in the Yeovil office, 1 day from home
- Enhanced Pension contribution + additional benefits available on request
- Some flexibility around school drop-off and pick-up, with an early finish on a Friday
- On-site parking
- The chance to develop within a finance function that is being built for the future

Why Apply?

This is a genuine opportunity to grow your finance career in a business that is investing in its team and processes. You'll gain broad, hands-on experience, learn from experienced finance professionals, and have real input into how the function improves.

title: Finance Administrator
description:
Finance Administrator (Accounts Payable)

Location: Yeovil, Somerset
Salary: £25,000 - £27,000 PA
Hours: Monday - Friday, 9am - 5pm (1 hour lunch)

Benefits
- 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays
- 5% Contributory Pension
- Free parking

Looking to build a career in finance?

We're recruiting for a Finance Administrator to join a friendly and supportive team of 7 in Yeovil. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with previous experience in accounts payable, finance, or administration, but we're also keen to hear from individuals who are naturally organised, enjoy working with numbers and data, and are looking to develop a career within finance.

If you're detail-oriented, proactive, and enjoy problem-solving, this could be a great next step for you.

The Role

As a Finance Administrator, you'll play an important role in supporting the day-to-day running of the finance department. You'll work closely with suppliers and colleagues across the business to ensure invoices, payments and financial records are processed accurately and efficiently.

This is a varied position where no two days are quite the same, offering plenty of opportunity to learn and develop your finance knowledge.

Key Responsibilities
- Processing and verifying supplier invoices
- Matching invoices to purchase orders and ensuring correct coding and approvals
- Preparing and assisting with supplier payment runs
- Monitoring payment deadlines and ensuring payments are made on time
- Investigating and resolving invoice queries and payment discrepancies
- Building positive relationships with suppliers and responding to enquiries
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving outstanding issues
- Maintaining accurate financial records and supporting finance administration tasks
- Working closely with colleagues across the business to support the wider finance function

About You

We're looking for someone who is:
- Organised with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable working with numbers, data and spreadsheets
- Confident communicating with colleagues, customers and suppliers
- Proactive and willing to learn
- Able to manage their workload effectively
- Reliable, positive and team-focused

Previous finance or accounts payable experience would be beneficial, but it's not essential. If you've worked in an administrative role, enjoy working with numbers, and are keen to develop a career in finance, we'd love to hear from you.

Don't Tick Every Box?

Please don't let that stop you from applying. We're interested in people with the right attitude, willingness to learn, and transferable skills just as much as direct experience. If this opportunity sounds like a good fit for you, we'd encourage you to apply.

How to Apply

To apply for this role, please do so online, email your CV to , or call Vicky on for a confidential chat.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Finance Assistant - Sales Ledger & Credit Control

Clevedon, UK

- Previous experience within a Sales Ledger, Accounts Receivable or Credit Control role
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel
- Experience using finance or ERP systems, ideally Microsoft Business Central
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workload effectively

This is an exciting time to join Hydro. As part of our "One Hydro" transformation programme, we're preparing for a new ERP implementation that will shape the future of our finance operations. You'll have the opportunity to work within a collaborative team environment and play a key role in supporting this business-wide change.

We offer the opportunity to grow your career within a global organisation that values innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.

Apply now and become part of the Hydro International team.

title: P/T ACCOUNTS ADMINISTRATOR / BOOKKEEPER
description:
ACCOUNTS ADMINISTRATOR / BOOKKEEPER

Somerset Solders Ltd, incorporating Somerset Workwear, is an established and growing Somerset business supplying customers across the electronics, construction, medical and transport sectors. We are an accredited Real Living Wage Employer and a Supporter of the West of England Good Employment Charter

This role is based at our Radstock site, we re open to discussing flexible start and finish times, compressed hours or part-time working. Please talk to us about what works for you.

We are looking for an experienced and dependable Accounts Administrator to join our small, friendly team. This is a varied, hands-on role with responsibility for the day-to-day accounting administration of the business.

We are offering a permanent position working 16 hours per week with a flexible approach on how the hours are worked with hybrid working to be discussed.

Key responsibilities as a accounts administrator / bookkeeper :
- Maintaining sales and purchase ledgers
- Credit control and customer statements
- Bank and nominal ledger reconciliations
- Resolving supplier and customer invoice queries
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns, ensuring VAT is correctly accounted for on transactions
- Liaising with colleagues, customers and suppliers on accounts matters
- Supporting month-end accounting processes / reporting to management
- Supporting our waste reduction, recycling and responsible sourcing practices in your day-to-day work.

You ll ideally have at least two years experience in bookkeeping or a similar accounting role and be comfortable working independently across a range of day-to-day accounting tasks. Experience with Xero is essential. Previous experience in working with an ERP system will be an advantage.

We offer you as a accounts administrator / bookkeeper:

You ll receive a full induction, ongoing training during paid working hours, opportunities for further professional development and regular one-to-ones coupled with an annual appraisal to support your development.
- Permanent part-time position 16 hours per week
- £25,00-£30,000 pro rata
- Flexible working hours to be discussed
- Opportunity for some hybrid working once established in the role
- Salary based on experience
- Company pension
- Free on-site parking
- Friendly, supportive small-team environment
- Training on the company ERP system
- Holiday entitlement increases with length of service
- We close between Christmas and New Year, usually around a week
- 20% staff discount off our products

If you would like to join us, please apply by emailing your CV for the attention of Caira Day

We welcome applications from everyone, regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation or background, and we particularly encourage applications from groups under-represented in our industry. title: Payroll and HR Administrator
description:
This varied role will involve payroll administration, maintaining HR records and systems, supporting employee life cycle processes, producing HR reports, and providing day-to-day support to managers and employees.

Client Details

FMCG - Frome

Description

We're looking for an organised and detail-oriented Payroll and HR Administrator to support the smooth day-to-day running of our HR and payroll activities. This is a varied position where you'll play a crucial role in ensuring employee records are accurate, payroll information is processed correctly, and colleagues across the business receive a high standard of support.

If you have previous payroll experience, excellent organisational skills, and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we'd love to hear from you.

As the Payroll and HR Administrator, you'll be responsible for:
- Supporting the accurate and timely processing of payroll information
- Maintaining employee data across HR, payroll, and Time & Attendance systems
- Ensuring employee records and documentation are accurate and up to date

- Preparing and processing HR documentation relating to recruitment, onboarding, training, performance reviews, grievances, and other employee matters
- Producing HR reports and supporting KPI data collection and analysis
- Managing absence records and supporting attendance management processes

Profile

To be successful in this role, you'll have:
- Previous Payroll & HR administration experience
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Experience using HR, payroll, or Time & Attendance systems
- Experience producing reports and analysing HR metrics/KPI data
- Strong IT, organisational, and administrative skills
- The ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- A customer-focused approach with excellent service skills
- The confidence to work independently and take ownership of tasks
- A flexible and adaptable mindset
- The ability to thrive in a busy, fast-paced environment
- A genuine interest in supporting people and delivering a great employee experience

Job Offer
- Salary up to 34k + Great benefits
- Opportunity to develop your HR and payroll expertise
- Varied and hands-on role with broad responsibilities
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- On-site 5 days a week - Frome

If you're an organised Payroll and HR Administrator looking for your next challenge in a people-focused business, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more about this opportunity based in Frome.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Citadel Source is partnering on an exclusive basis to support our client in the North East Somerset area in the recruitment of a Payroll Administrator to join their established payroll function. This is a fantastic opportunity to join a well-regarded organisation and play a key role in delivering an accurate, compliant, and efficient payroll service.

The role

We are seeking a detail-oriented Payroll Administrator to support the delivery of monthly payroll across a multi-site organisation. Working closely with the Payroll Lead, you will be responsible for processing payroll changes, maintaining payroll records, resolving payroll queries, and supporting payroll reporting and reconciliations. This role requires excellent organisational skills, a strong eye for detail, and the ability to work to strict payroll deadlines.

About you

You will ideally have previous payroll or payroll administration experience and be comfortable working with large volumes of data. You will possess strong organisational skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities. You will be confident communicating with stakeholders at all levels and enjoy working collaboratively within a busy team environment. Experience using payroll systems and Microsoft Office packages would be highly advantageous.

As a Payroll Administrator, your role will include, but not be limited to:
- Processing payroll changes including starters, leavers and contractual amendments
- Collating and validating monthly payroll data for submission to the payroll provider
- Processing overtime, expenses and additional payments accurately and on time
- Administering sickness, absence and statutory payroll payments
- Maintaining accurate and confidential payroll records
- Acting as a first point of contact for payroll, pension and tax-related queries
- Supporting payroll reconciliations and reporting activities
- Assisting with pension administration and submissions
- Working closely with HR, Finance and external payroll providers to ensure payroll accuracy

What the client has to offer
- Salary of £28,000 - £32,000 per annum
- Office-based
- Free on-site parking
- Generous annual leave entitlement
- Pension scheme
- Opportunity to join a supportive and collaborative team

Sound like a good fit?

If you are interested in discussing this role, please reach out to Harry Harvey at Citadel Source.

title: Payroll Officer
description:
Payroll Officer

Salary: 35,000 - 40,000 Location: North Somerset Hours: Full time or part time (22.5 hours minimum) considered

Are you an experienced payroll professional looking for a role where you can make a real impact?

Reed Payroll are delighted to be partnering with a well-established charity organisation in North Somerset to recruit a Payroll Officer. This is an excellent opportunity to join a values-driven organisation that provides vital services for the local community.

This role sits at the heart of both Finance and HR, offering much more variety than a traditional payroll position. Alongside taking ownership of payroll processing, you will have the opportunity to support payroll journals, reconciliations, pension administration and process improvement initiatives as the organisation continues to grow.

The organisation offers genuine flexibility and is focused on finding the right individual rather than fitting someone into a rigid working pattern.

The Role

As Payroll Officer, you will be responsible for delivering accurate and timely payroll services across weekly and monthly payroll cycles, while working closely with both Finance and HR colleagues.

Key responsibilities include:
- Processing weekly and monthly payrolls
- Managing payroll amendments including starters, leavers, salary changes and contractual updates
- Preparing payroll journals and reconciliations
- Administering workplace pension schemes and auto-enrolment processes
- Supporting salary sacrifice arrangements and employee benefits
- Maintaining accurate payroll records and ensuring compliance with payroll legislation
- Resolving payroll queries from employees and managers
- Producing payroll reports and supporting month-end processes
- Identifying opportunities to improve payroll processes, controls and efficiencies
- Working collaboratively with HR and Finance to ensure data accuracy and seamless payroll delivery
- This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys problem-solving, improving processes and being involved in wider business operations.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
- Previous end-to-end payroll experience
- Experience preparing payroll journals and reconciliations
- Strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation and statutory payments
- Pension administration experience, including auto-enrolment
- Experience working with salary sacrifice schemes
- Strong Excel skills and confidence working with manual payroll processes
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills
- The ability to build strong working relationships across Finance and HR teams
- A proactive mindset with a continuous improvement approach
- Experience within the charity or not-for-profit sector would be advantageous but is by no means essential.

What's in it for You?
- Salary of 35,000 - 40,000 depending on experience
- Flexible working arrangements tailored around the successful candidate
- 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata for part-time roles)
- Health Cash Plan
- Discounted gym membership
- Training and development opportunities
- Childcare discounts
- Employee assistance and counselling services
- Retail discount schemes
- The opportunity to join a friendly, supportive and purpose-driven organisation

If this sounds like the role for you, please apply online ASAP, successful applicants will be contacted within the next 24 working hours.
